extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A subset of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater. It includes tasks requiring multi-step reasoning, natural language understanding, world knowledge, and multilingual reasoning.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is curated from BIG-Bench by applying filtering criteria to select clean, challenging, and tractable tasks. The criteria include filtering out tasks with more than three subtasks, fewer than 103 examples, without human-rater baselines, not using multiple-choice or exact match evaluation, and where the best reported model beats the average human-rater score. After manual inspection, 23 tasks were selected as BIG-Bench Hard.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data is sourced from BIG-Bench, a diverse evaluation suite with over 200 text-based tasks. The tasks are crowd-sourced and include traditional NLP, mathematics, commonsense reasoning, and question-answering.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Filtering criteria were applied to BIG-Bench tasks to create a clean subset. For all but three tasks in BBH, a random subset of 250 evaluation examples was taken. For Causal Judgement, Penguins in a Table, and Snarks, all available test examples were considered.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Examples were reserved for few-shot prompting (3 examples) and evaluation (100 or more examples). The benchmark includes 6,511 evaluation examples in total. Prompt lengths were adjusted for different models (e.g., 1,000 tokens for Geometric Shapes, 512 for most tasks with OpenAI models, 2,048 input length for PaLM).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-rater baselines were established by the BIG-Bench organizers, who enlisted a team of raters to manually solve each task and score them against golden labels. The human-evaluation component took almost a year, with raters allocated a few hours per day to solve a sub-sampled evaluation set, using external resources like the Internet.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The human-rater scores are not fully representative of human performance due to changes in task formatting and content over time, and some tasks had hard-to-follow descriptions. The average and maximum human-rater performances are reported, but should be interpreted with care.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The data, prompts, and Codex model outputs are available at https://github.com/suzgunmirac/BIG-Bench-Hard. No versioning, updating timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policies are specified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses that surpassing average human-rater performance on challenging tasks should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning, highlighting limitations in interpreting model capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Some tasks require knowledge about common practices and presuppositions in Western society (e.g., Causal Judgement, Ruin Names). The human-rater baselines may not be representative of the entire population.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The human-rater performance is not fully representative due to changes in task formatting and content over time. Some tasks are extremely difficult and require domain-specific knowledge or are not practically solvable within twenty minutes. The benchmark focuses on tasks that are challenging but tractable with current prompting methods.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for evaluating few-shot prompting and chain-of-thought prompting in language models. It is intended for testing model capabilities on challenging tasks, with usage in training, testing, and validation of language models. The paper provides prompts and evaluation protocols for reproducibility.
